page: Amazon Web Services m7i.xlarge is a general-purpose server instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture with a dedicated Intel Xeon 8488C processor operating at 3.2 GHz. The configuration includes 4 vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The system is equipped with 16.0 GB of DDR5 memory running at 5 GHz, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core. The processor features a 105 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets, including Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX-512) and Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for tile and int8 operations. No local storage or GPU hardware is bundled with this instance, and it provides a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks show a distinct contrast between single-core and multi-core capabilities. The instance demonstrates strong single-core performance, highlighted by a Geekbench single-core score of 2097.0 and high single-threaded gzip compression speeds of 33.37 GB/sec. However, multi-core and memory-intensive operations represent a relative tradeoff. Multi-core CPU performance under stress-ng and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression fall into the lower performance tier. Memory bandwidth tests, such as uncached large block reads and writes, also register in the bottom quartile, alongside weaker database and Redis SET operations.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the m7i.xlarge offers a balanced resource density suitable for workloads that require modern instruction sets without demanding high memory bandwidth or local storage. It is well-suited for applications such as static web serving, single-threaded text processing, and light machine learning inference, as demonstrated by its average performance in prompt processing and text generation with small and medium models. It is less optimal for heavy database operations, software compilation, or highly parallelized multi-threaded computing.
